title: Project Drive's backend is assembled; launch remains gated
summary: The storage, access, upload, handover, and cleanup paths are assembled on the feature branch, while final integrated verification, customer UI, and every production gate remain open.
businessMeaning: The feasibility risk is closed. Signal Studio can focus investment on making ownership and access easy to understand, while separate founder approvals prevent unfinished UI, policy, database, or operational work from reaching customers.

decisions.question: Which Connections direction should become the production experience?
decisions.recommendation: Select A · Custodian, then name any zones 1–5 to carry forward.
decisions.why: It is the clearest Signal fit: ownership, reassurance, and recovery remain human and understandable without turning a simple connection into an administration console.

risks.impact: Customers cannot connect Drive, understand storage ownership, or use the new path through the product.
risks.mitigation: Select one thesis and any zones, then build and verify every registered state at all four breakpoints.

risks.title: Production approvals must remain independent
risks.impact: Bundling legal, database, deployment, or worker decisions could advance a change without the evidence required for a safe launch.
risks.mitigation: Keep privacy wording, migrations 0028 and 0029, deployment, and each repair-worker activation as separate founder gates.

risks.title: Windows libSQL teardown can obscure local test results
risks.impact: Exit 3221225477 can make completed logical assertions appear as an aggregate process failure.
risks.mitigation: Record assertion-level results, preserve the exit as a failure, and treat Linux CI as release authority.

technicalReceipt.summary: Durable implementation facts for engineering review; none authorizes a production action.
items: Customer UI uses Connections, Who can open this board's files, and Resources. Project Drive remains an internal project name.
The OAuth request set is exactly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file; no identity, full-Drive, or read-only-Drive scope is requested.
One current personal Drive connection may support several boards. Each board names one current storage owner.
Drive upload readiness requires an exact current-email writer receipt for every current non-owner member.
The configured Drive and Blob paths send bytes browser-to-provider. A no-Blob fallback remains a separate 3 MB server path.
The customer upload ceiling is 50 MB. Live in-product 50 MB, killed-browser, full-Drive, disconnect, and recovery acceptance remain pending.
Drive resources open Google's verified webViewLink in a new tab; the product does not embed the Drive viewer.
Four tables carry the model: provider_connections, workspace_storage, drive_folder_grants, and project_drive_operations.
Exact Signal-native cleanup receipts reuse meta and never authorize a prefix deletion or deletion of Drive-owned bytes.
Migrations 0028 and 0029 passed disposable local apply, no-op, integrity, and contract checks. Neither local evidence nor this report authorizes production migration.
Four independently selected count-only repair paths default off: revoke, grant creation, folder repair, and native-byte cleanup.
The two-account result is a live Google sharing spike, not the still-pending in-product customer lifecycle.
Final integrated branch results and the final pull-request head are intentionally not claimed while their status entries remain pending.
No privacy wording, pricing, production migration, deployment, or repair-worker activation is authorized by this report.
